questions.prompt: Why did Aiden go home feeling upset?
choices: Marcus kept calling him a silly name.
Betty would not speak to him.
He had lost Socks at school.
questions.answer: Marcus kept calling him a silly name.
questions.rationale: Marcus kept calling Aiden a silly name, and the next page says Aiden went home upset, so the repeated name-calling caused his upset feelings.
questions.evidenceText: He kept calling Aiden a silly name. Aiden did not like it.

supportingEvidence.evidenceText: Aiden went home feeling quiet and upset.

questions.prompt: What plan helped Aiden respond to the bullying?
choices: Call Marcus a name, then hide from the class.
Speak clearly, walk away, and tell Miss Okafor.
Stay silent, leave school, and solve it alone.
questions.answer: Speak clearly, walk away, and tell Miss Okafor.
questions.rationale: Aiden planned to speak clearly, walk away, and tell Miss Okafor; pages 7 and 8 show him doing each step when Marcus used the name again, so the plan guided his response.
questions.evidenceText: He would speak clearly, walk away, and tell Miss Okafor.

supportingEvidence.evidenceText: Aiden faced him. "My name is Aiden. Stop," he said in a clear voice.
Aiden walked away with Betty. They told Miss Okafor what had happened.

questions.prompt: What is the most important lesson about bullying?
choices: Bullying ends if you ignore every adult.
questions.evidenceText: "Bullying is never your fault." Aiden remembered her words.
